validated_results.title: Identification of metabolites associated with prostate cancer risk: a nested case-control study with long follow-up in the Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study.
validated_results.reason: This nested case-control study reports prospective relative risk estimates for circulating glycine concentrations and incident prostate cancer risk.

extraction.population: Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study (NSHDS)

sample_size.location: Methods, Study design, paragraph 5; total_n derived from reported group counts 333 + 333 = 666

cases.excerpt: Because of the lower prevalence of prostate cancer in younger participants, we included 40- and 50-year-olds in the same subgroup (younger, 40–50 years, n = 333 sets), while 60-year-olds were included in another subgroup (older, 60 years, n = 444 sets).

comparison.excerpt: The metabolite concentrations were log 2 -transformed, and thus, linear estimates were per doubling.

design.excerpt: In a case-control study nested in the Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study, pre-diagnostic concentrations of 148 plasma metabolites were determined

timing.excerpt: This study investigated the prospective association between plasma metabolite concentrations and prostate cancer risk

continent.excerpt: The NSHDS is a population-based cohort that started in 1985 [ 20 ]. In brief, residents in the Swedish province of Västerbotten were invited to a health assessment
continent.location: Methods, The Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study, paragraph 1

location.excerpt: nested in the Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Plasma samples were analysed using both targeted MS- and NMR-based metabolomics
